Your conscription physical put you in the supplementary reserve, and you are called up as a home-defence conscript (bangwi). After a few weeks of training you will commute from home to a unit or the neighbourhood office and serve about {0} months.

Your service medical put you in the supplementary reserve, and you are called up as a social service worker. After basic military training you will commute from home to a care facility or public office and serve about {0} months.
In 1990, of about 450,000 men liable for service, 200,000 went to active duty, 120,000 were called up as home-defence conscripts (bangwi) and 130,000 were exempted (Seoul Shinmun, 1991).

Before discharge

Your unit encouraged you to apply to become a sergeant. If you are accepted, you will go through NCO training and be appointed a sergeant, a career soldier with a salary. After four years, if you are chosen for long-term service, you can stay in the army until retirement age.
Of NCOs on short-term service, about 25% were chosen for long-term service in 2010 and about 20% in 2026 (Seoul Shinmun, Money Today).
